title: AI-Driven Early Warning System for Oceanic Dead Zones
summary: VIT is developing a system to forecast ocean hypoxia two to four weeks ahead, with regional pilots planned.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: The prototype combines environmental data with neural models to predict low-oxygen conditions. Proposed pilots cover hypoxia-prone seas, and intended responses include nutrient management and fishing restrictions. The source does not document an actual alert-driven intervention, avoided fish mortality, or preserved fishing income.
purpose: Provide advance warning of marine hypoxia to support timely management.
system: AI-Driven Early Warning System for Oceanic Dead Zones
location: Gulf of Mexico, Bay of Bengal, and Arabian Sea (planned pilots)

ratings.reason: The ocean dead-zone system is a prototype and regional pilots are planned; named agencies are not evidence of operational impact.
Preserved fishing livelihoods are expected, not documented.
No actual hypoxia alert, intervention, or ecosystem benefit is reported.

ai_role.statement: The contributor describes the system and its proposed or reported contribution. This collection entry does not independently isolate the effect of AI from the surrounding workflow.

evidence.citation: Contributed use case in International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact, 2025. Information current as of June 2025. The reported outcomes are attributed to the submitting project, not an independent outcome evaluation by ITU.
evidence.title: Use Case 16: AI-Driven Early Warning System for Oceanic Dead Zones

produced_by: The contributor describes the application and its setting in the cited entry. Conditions sufficient to reproduce the reported benefit have not been established.
must_hold: Requirements for reproducing the benefit need to be evaluated in the new setting. The collection entry does not establish that its reported results will recur.
